spec.description: What the tags are costing you. A transaction has exactly one category but any number of tags, which is how this dashboard can answer what a whole trip cost across groceries, fuel and lodging at once, or how much of this month's spending is coming back as a reimbursement. Tags are added by hand in SQL: SELECT tag_transaction(id, 'tag'); the id is in the tables at the bottom. Everything here honours the time picker. Note that the per-tag figures do not add up to your total spending, and should not: a transaction with two tags is counted under both.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(v.outflow) AS "Tagged spending"
FROM v_spending v
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                     JOIN tags tg ON tg.id = tt.tag_id
                    WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id
                      AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[])))

spec.description: Money out on transactions carrying any selected tag. Counted once per transaction however many tags it has. HONOURS the time picker, like every panel here.
spec.title: Tagged Spending

spec.rawSql:
SELECT tag AS "Tag",
       category_path AS "Category",
       transactions  AS "Transactions",
       spend         AS "Spent"
FROM v_tag_category
WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tag = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY tag, spend DESC

spec.description: The same breakdown as the donut, read as a list and across every selected tag at once. All-time: v_tag_category is not time-filtered, so this is the full history of each tag.
spec.title: Tags & Trees

spec.rawSql:
SELECT tag AS "Tag",
       also_tagged  AS "Also tagged",
       transactions AS "Transactions"
FROM v_tag_overlap
WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tag = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY transactions DESC, tag

spec.description: Pairs of tags on the same transaction. Usually that is deliberate - a client trip is both reimbursable and part of the trip - and occasionally it is how a tagging slip shows up. Each pair appears twice, once from each side.
spec.title: Proximal Tags

spec.rawSql:
SELECT v.id AS "id",
       to_char(v.posted_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "Date",
       v.account   AS "Account",
       coalesce(v.merchant, v.description, v.raw_description) AS "Merchant",
       coalesce(v.category_path, 'Uncategorized') AS "Category",
       tt.tag_list AS "Tags",
       v.amount    AS "Amount"
FROM v_transactions v
JOIN v_transaction_tags tt ON tt.transaction_id = v.id
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                     JOIN tags tg ON tg.id = tt.tag_id
                    WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id
                      AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[])))
ORDER BY v.posted_on DESC, v.amount

spec.description: Every tagged transaction in range, newest first. Amount is signed: negative left your accounts, positive arrived. The id column is the one to copy into untag_transaction(id, 'tag') when a tag is wrong. Joined through v_transaction_tags, so a transaction with three tags appears once with all three listed rather than three times.
spec.title: Tagged Transactions

spec.rawSql:
SELECT v.id AS "id",
       to_char(v.posted_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "Date",
       v.account   AS "Account",
       coalesce(v.merchant, v.description, v.raw_description) AS "Merchant",
       coalesce(v.category_path, 'Uncategorized') AS "Category",
       v.outflow   AS "Amount"
FROM v_spending v
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                          WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id)
ORDER BY v.outflow DESC
LIMIT 50

spec.description: The working list for tagging by hand: the biggest spending with no tag yet. Copy an id and run SELECT tag_transaction(id, 'your-tag'); - the tag is created if it is new, and running it twice is harmless. Ignores the tag selector, since nothing here has a tag.
spec.title: Untagged Transactions

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(v.inflow) AS "Came back"
FROM v_transactions v
WHERE NOT v.is_internal AND $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                     JOIN tags tg ON tg.id = tt.tag_id
                    WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id
                      AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[])))

spec.description: Money arriving on tagged transactions - a refund, a reimbursement, a shared cost settled up. This is the half a category tree cannot connect to the spending it offsets.
spec.title: Tagged Income

spec.rawSql:
WITH t AS (
    SELECT coalesce(sum(v.outflow) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.is_internal), 0) AS out,
           coalesce(sum(v.inflow)  FILTER (WHERE NOT v.is_internal), 0) AS back
    FROM v_transactions v
    WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                     JOIN tags tg ON tg.id = tt.tag_id
                    WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id
                      AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[])))
)
SELECT out - back AS "Net cost" FROM t

spec.description: What the selected tags actually cost once anything that came back is taken off. Negative means more returned than went out.
spec.title: Net cost

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "Transactions"
FROM v_transactions v
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                     JOIN tags tg ON tg.id = tt.tag_id
                    WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id
                      AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[])))

spec.description: How many transactions carry a selected tag.
spec.title: Transactions

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(v.outflow) AS "Untagged"
FROM v_spending v
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                          WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id)

spec.description: Spending with no tag at all. Ignores the tag selector - it is the backlog, and the honest denominator for everything above. Tagging is by hand, so this never reaches zero on its own.
spec.title: Untagged Spending

spec.rawSql:
SELECT tg.name AS "Tag",
       coalesce(sum(v.outflow) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.is_internal), 0)
         - coalesce(sum(v.inflow) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.is_internal), 0)
           AS "Net cost"
FROM tags tg
JOIN transaction_tags tt ON tt.tag_id = tg.id
JOIN v_transactions v    ON v.id = tt.transaction_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[]))
GROUP BY tg.name
ORDER BY 2 DESC

spec.description: Net cost per tag, biggest first. Each bar is independent: a transaction with two tags counts toward both, so the bars do not add up to your total spending and are not meant to.
spec.title: Tag Net Cost

spec.rawSql:
WITH per_tag AS (
    SELECT tg.name AS tag, tg.note,
           count(*)                                        AS transactions,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.is_internal)            AS internal,
           coalesce(sum(v.outflow) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.is_internal), 0) AS spend,
           coalesce(sum(v.inflow)  FILTER (WHERE NOT v.is_internal), 0) AS back,
           count(DISTINCT v.category_id)                    AS categories,
           count(DISTINCT date_trunc('month', v.posted_on)) AS months,
           min(v.posted_on) AS first_seen,
           max(v.posted_on) AS last_seen
    FROM tags tg
    JOIN transaction_tags tt ON tt.tag_id = tg.id
    JOIN v_transactions v    ON v.id = tt.transaction_id
    WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[]))
    GROUP BY tg.name, tg.note
)
SELECT tag AS "Tag",
       coalesce(note, '') AS "Means",
       transactions AS "Transactions",
       spend        AS "Spent",
       back         AS "Came back",
       spend - back AS "Net",
       categories   AS "Categories",
       months       AS "Months",
       to_char(first_seen, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "First",
       to_char(last_seen,  'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "Last"
FROM per_tag
UNION ALL
SELECT 'No tags in this range', '', NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL,
       NULL, NULL
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM per_tag)
ORDER BY 6 DESC NULLS LAST

spec.description: One row per tag. Means is the tag's note - worth filling in for anything you will still be using in a year (UPDATE tags SET note = '...'). Categories counts how many different categories the tag reaches, which is the clearest sign a tag is doing work a category could not. HONOURS the time picker, like every panel here.
spec.title: Tags

spec.rawSql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT (month::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/Denver') AS t,
           tag, spend
    FROM v_tag_monthly
)
SELECT t AS "time", tag AS metric, spend AS value
FROM m
WHERE $__timeFilter(t) AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tag = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY 1, 2

spec.description: One series per tag. Reads from v_tag_monthly, which is already grouped by tag and month, so nothing fans out. A tag for a one-off trip shows as a single spike; a standing tag like reimbursable shows a rhythm. Not account-filtered.
spec.title: Monthly Tag Spending

spec.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(v.category_path, 'Uncategorized') AS metric,
       sum(v.outflow) AS value
FROM v_spending v
WHERE $__timeFilter(v."time") AND (array_length(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR account = ANY(ARRAY[${account:sqlstring}]::text[])) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_tags tt
                     JOIN tags tg ON tg.id = tt.tag_id
                    WHERE tt.transaction_id = v.id
                      AND (array_length(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR tg.name = ANY(ARRAY[${tag:sqlstring}]::text[])))
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

spec.description: Where the tagged money landed in the category tree. This is the question tags exist for: one trip spread across travel, groceries and utilities shows here as three slices, while the category tree can only ever show it as three unrelated expenses.
spec.title: Tags by Category
